Packages.Name: bff
Packages.Doc:
Package bff is the backend-for-frontend for the Model Bank apps.

It is the only server the thin clients talk to. It owns sessions and login,
and turns banking data into screen-ready trees (package screen). Apart from
health, the public login screen and login itself, every endpoint requires a
session; the customer identity always comes from the session, never from
the request.

The banking core is reached through the core package's CustomerQueries and
Authenticator contracts (ADR-0002).

Packages.Name: staff
Packages.Doc:
Package staff is the staff web of the Model Bank: the login (story
1.7.1), the pages a member of staff reads the bank through (accounting,
products, customers, payments, treasury, reports, about and the
documentation), the role the signed-in user holds and the PII
authorisation that gate what they see, the layout every page is
rendered in, and the simulation console when there is one (ADR-0002
stage 6, stories 1.6.3 and 1.6.4).

It reads the bank through core.StaffQueries, acts on it through
core.Commands, checks logins through core.Users and drives the
simulation through Console, and knows nothing else of it. The BFF mounts
it beside the customer routes (bff.Config.Staff) and its sessions are
kept in the BFF's store.

Registrars.Name: NewServer
Registrars.Doc:
Builds the handler. Every route except /v1/health, GET
/v1/screen/login and POST /v1/login requires a valid session.

Registrars.Name: (*Site).consoleRoutes
Registrars.Doc:
Mounts the simulation console: the dashboard and its
controls, the payments generator, the settings, the runtime, export and
import, the explorer and the status another program reads.

Registrars.Name: (*Site).loginRoutes
Registrars.Doc: Mounts the login page and the logout.

Registrars.Name: (*Site).movementRoutes
Registrars.Doc:
Serves the movement page, its goluca text and JSON, and
the WASM assets.

Registrars.Name: (*Site).routes
Registrars.Doc:
Mounts the staff pages: accounting, products, customers,
payments, treasury, reports and about, and the PII authorisation.

Registrars.Name: (*Site).viewRoutes
Registrars.Doc:
Mounts the view switch: GET view/{name}?back=<path> sets
the cookie and returns to the page that offered it.

Routes.Doc: Every other path under /v1/: not_found, as JSON.
Answers as soon as the process serves HTTP. No session.

Checks the customer ID and password, from a JSON body or a form,
and opens a session: a JSON client gets the token and the home screen; a
form post or a browser gets the mb_session cookie and is sent to the
home screen. Five failures for one customer ID or from one address in
fifteen minutes lock that key for the rest of the window (429 with
Retry-After).

Ends the session: a browser's cookie is cleared and it is sent
to the login screen; a JSON client gets the login screen.

Serves the API document (package api): the surface this server
and the staff web present, as built.

The home screen: the customer's net position and a row per
account, each opening its product screen.

The customer's transactions across every account, newest
first, one page (?page=) at a time.

The front door: the login form, whose submit is POST
/v1/login, with the deployment's note. No session.

One account, by its index in the customer's list: its
details and its own transactions, one page (?page=) at a time; 404 for
an index the customer has no account at.

The dashboard: the bank's position, the run's state and its controls;
it polls its own sections.
The project: what the Model Bank is, its aims and its non-goals.

The demo's state for another program (GET, no session): version,
schema, settings, the run and its rates, the position and the restart
record. gobank-deploy's upgrade drill reads it before and after each
redeploy; a performance run reads the rates.
The architecture decision records compiled into this build.

The API: every route the BFF and the staff web serve, read off the
code at build time (package api), in sections by where each is
registered, each linking to its own page; the types the bodies
are made of follow. The OpenAPI document is at v1/openapi.json.
A static page: the surface does not change while the run goes.

One route of the API: what its handler needs, reads and answers,
with a link to the registration in the source at this build's tag.
The method is the pattern's or "any", the path the pattern's.

The system documentation: the component registry, who may read what,
the pre-rule debt and the ADR list.

An ADR whole: its page, or one of the diagrams and sources its
markdown names beside it.
The architecture models: the C4 system context and container diagrams.

Runtime: the process, its memory against the limit, the schema
versions and the restart record.
The balance sheet on the current business day, with the CET1 position.

The profit and loss statement since the bank opened, on an accrual
basis.

Opens n customers in the background (POST n=), with the product mix
the simulation uses; /about.json shows the batch's rate.
Runs one business day while the run is stopped (POST).

PII (POST): an admin authorises themselves to see personal data for a
while, then returns to redirect=.

PII (POST): the admin gives the authorisation up and returns to
redirect=.

The customers, one page (?page=) at a time; personal data only for an
authorised admin.

Under /customers/: a customer's detail at /customers/{id}, or one of
their accounts at /customers/{id}/account/{index}, each with its
transactions one page (?txpage=) at a time.

Customer search by name (POST name=): the customers whose name
contains it, oldest first and at most core.CustomerSearchLimit, as the
register's table — the matches alone for htmx, the Customers page
with them for a browser. The name is personal data: it travels in the
body and never in a URL, and only an authorised admin may search.
The dashboard's polled sections, as an HTML fragment.
Events: the record of what happened and what it caused (ADR-0011)
The whole book as a .goluca file (GET): admin only.
The tab icon as .ico, from lofigui.
Unknowns: handler lofigui.ServeFavicon: body outside the walk

Routes.Doc: The tab icon as SVG.

Replaces the book with an uploaded .goluca file (POST, multipart
file=): admin only.

The DB explorer: every component's tables, read-only; a role sees only
the components it may (customers needs view_pii).
The DB explorer's tables and rows, under its prefix.

The staff login: the form (GET) and its check (POST login, password)
against the users component. Five failures for one login or from one
address lock it for fifteen minutes; 503 on a deployment with no users.

Responses.Note: Staff login is not set up on this deployment.

Routes.Doc:
Ends the staff session (POST): the cookie is cleared and the browser
sent to the login page.

One movement of the ledger (ADR-0008): its page; with the suffix
.goluca its plain-text-accounting text, with .json the movement itself.

Payments: the list, newest first, one page (?page=) at a time, with
the generator's controls.
Starts the payment generator (POST): the settings' payments a day.
Sends one generated payment now (POST).
Stops the payment generator (POST).
One payment: its detail and the movements it made.

The bank's own parameters (Bank Rate, the reserve ratio and the rest),
as the Bank tab shows them.

The lending products: the family's catalogue, each product with its
book.

The savings products: the family's catalogue, each product with its
book.

The BBSI return (Bank and Building Society Interest): each customer's
interest for the year; personal data only for an authorised admin.
The charts: the book, the customer count and the rates over the run.

A customer as the app shows them (?id=); without an id, the customer
list.

Empties the bank and starts again on its opening day (POST); the
settings are kept.

The console settings: the page (GET), and the change (POST
max_customers, payments_per_day, day_length; 0s runs flat out, a day
length that does not parse leaves the current one). The day length set
here is the run's and outlives the process.

The settings page's status line, polled on its own so the form is
never re-rendered under the operator.

Starts the run (POST): the simulation moves day after day at the
settings' day length until stopped.
Stops the run after the day in progress (POST).
The reserve ratio against its requirement, and the lending headroom.

The cash position: deposits, loans, cash at the BoE against the
required reserves, and the Bank Rate.
The gilt holdings and the purchase form.

Buys a gilt (POST tenor, face_value in pounds): admin only; returns to
the gilts page.

Switches this browser between the bank's view and the customer's:
sets the staff_view cookie for a year and returns to ?back=.

pta2svg's browser renderer and its loader, embedded (ADR-0008), so the
movement page draws in the tab.

Gates.Doc:
requireLogin serves the open paths as they are and every other with the
session the request's cookie names, or sends the browser to the login
page with the page it wanted to come back to. An HTMX request that has
lost its session is told to load the login page whole.

Types.Name: bff.errorBody
Types.Doc:
errorBody is every error as a JSON client gets it: a stable code to
switch on, what to tell the customer, and the screen to show with it
when there is one (the login screen with its notice).

Fields.Name: error
Fields.Doc: bad_request, unauthenticated, bad_credentials, rate_limited, not_found or internal

Types.Name: bff.loginResponse
Types.Doc:
loginResponse is what a JSON client gets for a login: the session token
to send back as a bearer, when the session ends whatever happens (it
also ends after fifteen idle minutes), and the home screen, so the
client has nothing more to fetch.

Fields.Name: expires_at
Fields.Doc: RFC 3339, UTC

Types.Name: bff.screenBody
Types.Doc: screenBody is a screen on its own, as the logout answers a JSON client.

Types.Name: core.EventRecord
Types.Doc:
EventRecord is one event on the bank's record (ADR-0011): something
that happened at an instant, raised by someone, whose cascade is
pending or done.

Fields.Name: Kind
Fields.Doc: "start of day", "publication", "payment", "setting", "opening"

Fields.Name: Status
Fields.Doc: "pending", "done"

Fields.Name: By
Fields.Doc: who raised it: a user, a customer, a market's name, "clock"

Types.Name: core.Leg
Types.Doc:
Leg is one side of a movement: the account and the balance it was left
with, signed as the ledger holds it.

Fields.Name: Path
Fields.Doc: "Liability:Savings:cust-001:easy-access"

Fields.Name: Type
Fields.Doc: the path's first segment: Asset, Liability, Equity, Income, Expense

Types.Name: core.Movement
Types.Doc:
Movement is one ledger movement as written (ADR-0008): a signed amount
from one account to another, the to account's balance rising by it and
the from account's falling, with the balance each is left with, in the
bank's view.

Fields.Name: Cause
Fields.Doc:
Cause is the root event a rule's posting was made under (ADR-0011)
and Step the posting's name within it; nil and empty for a movement
that is not a rule's, or from before the record.

Types.Name: screen.Action
Types.Doc:
Action is what happens when the user taps a component. Exactly one of the
fields is set.

Fields.Name: screen
Fields.Doc: GET this path and show the result

Fields.Name: submit
Fields.Doc: POST form values to this path

Fields.Name: logout
Fields.Doc: end the session

Types.Name: screen.Component
Types.Doc:
Component is one element of a screen body. Type selects the component and
which of the other fields are meaningful; unused fields are omitted from
JSON.

Fields.Name: currency
Fields.Doc: ISO 4217 code of the money a row or tx shows; the renderer picks the glyph by it

Types.Name: screen.Field
Types.Doc: Field is one input in a form.

Fields.Name: kind
Fields.Doc: "text", "password", "number"

Types.Name: screen.Icon
Types.Doc: Icon names a glyph. Clients map icons to their icon set.

Types.Name: screen.Nav
Types.Doc: Nav is the bottom tab bar.

Types.Name: screen.Pair
Types.Doc: Pair is a label/value line inside a hero or details component.

Types.Name: screen.Screen
Types.Doc: Screen is one app view.

Fields.Name: path
Fields.Doc: GET path that returns this screen

Types.Name: screen.Tab
Types.Doc: Tab is one entry in the bottom tab bar.

Types.Name: screen.Tone
Types.Doc: Tone selects a colour treatment. Clients map tones to their theme.

Types.Name: staff.AboutOwed
Types.Doc: AboutOwed is core.Owed as another program reads it.

Fields.Name: events
Fields.Doc: root events due and not done: cascades in progress (ADR-0011)

Types.Name: staff.AboutPosition
Types.Doc: AboutPosition is the bank's position: what the dashboard leads with.

Fields.Name: day
Fields.Doc: YYYY-MM-DD

Fields.Name: savings
Fields.Doc: formatted, as the dashboard shows it

Types.Name: staff.AboutRestart
Types.Doc:
AboutRestart is one row of the restart record, newest first, read with
the row before it (see Restart).

Fields.Name: previous_version
Fields.Doc: "" for unrecorded or none

Fields.Name: downtime
Fields.Doc: Go duration; "" when unknown

Fields.Name: intact
Fields.Doc: day and customers equal across the stop; null when the previous row cannot say

Types.Name: staff.AboutRoute
Types.Doc:
AboutRoute is one route's figures since the process started, as
internal/routestats keeps them: the count, the latency (last, p50 and
p95 of the latest requests, the maximum ever), the most in flight at
once and the rate over the last minute.

Fields.Name: pattern
Fields.Doc: as registered: "GET /v1/health"

Fields.Name: last
Fields.Doc: Go durations

Fields.Name: per_second
Fields.Doc: completed in the last minute, a second

Types.Name: staff.AboutSettings
Types.Doc: AboutSettings are the console settings.

Fields.Name: day_length
Fields.Doc: Go duration; "0s" is flat out

Types.Name: staff.AboutSim
Types.Doc:
AboutSim is the run as it is now, with the two rates a performance run
reads: customers added per second (the live rate while a batch add runs,
else the last batch's) and account days per 12h at the pass's measured
whole-day rate, with the last day it is made of.

Fields.Name: wall
Fields.Doc: the wall clock now, RFC 3339 UTC

Fields.Name: clock
Fields.Doc: the bank's clock now (simulated time), RFC 3339 UTC

Fields.Name: warp
Fields.Doc: simulated seconds per wall second; 0 when flat out

Fields.Name: day_ends_in
Fields.Doc: Go duration; "0s" when flat out or stopped

Fields.Name: last_day_duration
Fields.Doc: Go duration; "" before the first day

Fields.Name: day_refused
Fields.Doc: why the bank would not follow the clock when last asked

Fields.Name: owed
Fields.Doc: what the bank owed when last asked (ADR-0010); a drill waits for at_rest

Fields.Name: next_event
Fields.Doc: the event the run loop waits for: "payment at 2020-03-04T10:32:00Z"

Types.Name: staff.AboutStatus
Types.Doc:
AboutStatus is the demo's state as another program reads it, at
/about.json: the version and schema this process runs, the console
settings, the run's position and the restart record. gobank-deploy's
upgrade drill reads it before and after each redeploy to compare the
position and read the downtime off the newest restart row.

Fields.Name: routes
Fields.Doc: what the process has measured of each route it served

Types.Name: staff.SchemaVersion
Types.Doc: SchemaVersion is the version a component's tables are at.

Types.Name: time.Time
Types.Doc: RFC 3339
